sweet-bean-2015.gazette: Japan segregated people with Hansen's disease into state sanatoria for most of the twentieth century, and the law authorizing it stayed on the books until 1996. Tokue's decades of confinement are not a backstory device; they are the ordinary shape of a life lived under that statute. Many residents stayed in the sanatoria long after repeal, there being nowhere else that would take them.

tangerine-2015.gazette: Baker shot on and around Santa Monica Boulevard with three iPhones and without the apparatus that usually announces a film crew. His leads were trans women from that world who shaped their own dialogue and their characters' logic, credited as performers rather than consulted as subjects. The realism here is contractual: the film borrows its credibility from people who had to keep living in the neighbourhood after the crew left.

the-big-short-2015.gazette: The instruments the film names were real products with real desks behind them — subprime mortgage bonds, collateralized debt obligations, credit default swaps written against both. Its investors are compressed and recombined, but the trades follow the documented record: a few outsiders read the underlying loan tapes, found them rotten, and bought insurance on a market rated safe. Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy in September 2008, and no one in that record had stopped it.
the-big-short-2015.prism: Betting correctly against a fraud isn't the same as opposing it. The payout required the collapse to arrive on schedule, which means the film's heroes needed the foreclosures as much as the banks did.

the-revenant-2015.gazette: Iñárritu shot in sequence and in natural light, which left a narrow usable window each day and stretched the schedule until the Alberta snow gave out and the production moved to southern Argentina to finish. Crew departures, budget overruns and the cold were all being reported while the film was still shooting. The claims and the counter-claims are checkable against the production record, which is where the argument about this film has lived ever since.

the-witch-2015.gazette: Eggers assembled the film out of 17th-century sources — diaries, sermons, and trial transcripts — with lines of dialogue lifted from testimony given by people who believed every word of it. The farmhouse was raised with period methods and the family's speech kept its archaic grammar rather than being smoothed toward modern English. Nothing in the folklore was softened for the audience: the film runs the beliefs of 1630 New England as the operating physics of its world.

dangal-2016.gazette: Mahavir Singh Phogat trained his daughters on a dirt pit in a Haryana village at a time when women's wrestling had almost no institutional foothold in the state. Geeta Phogat won gold at the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi, the first Indian woman to take a Commonwealth wrestling title, and Babita followed with medals of her own. The film stages those bouts closely enough that the record can be laid down beside it, round for round.
dangal-2016.prism: The regimen the film frames as sacrifice was imposed on children who were never asked. Dangal holds both facts at once — the medals are real, and so is the fact that somebody else decided what those girls' bodies were for.

hacksaw-ridge-2016.gazette: Desmond Doss enlisted as a combat medic and refused to carry a weapon, and the Army spent months trying to court-martial or discharge him before it ever reached Okinawa. On the Maeda Escarpment in May 1945 he remained on the cliff after his unit had withdrawn, lowering wounded men down the rock face by rope through the night. He became the first conscientious objector to receive the Medal of Honor, and the citation is a public document.

hidden-figures-2016.gazette: Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson worked at NASA's Langley under Virginia segregation law, in a computing pool designated West Area for precisely that reason. Johnson's orbital calculations preceded John Glenn's Friendship 7 flight in February 1962. The film composites several of its administrators into people who never existed; the three women, the segregated facilities and the launch are all matters of record.

i-daniel-blake-2016.gazette: Loach and Paul Laverty spent months with claimants, welfare advisers and food bank staff across northern England before shooting in Newcastle. The work capability assessment, the sanction, the digital-by-default application — each procedure in the film was drawn from a system operating in exactly that form at the time. The realism is the claim being staked: the film puts itself up for checking against the benefits office rather than against other films.
i-daniel-blake-2016.prism: A drama can always be dismissed as a drama, and that's the cost of the contract. Loach traded documentary's authority for reach, which left the officials he described free to answer that it was, after all, made up.

maudie-2016.gazette: Maud Lewis painted out of a one-room house near Digby, Nova Scotia, small enough that the work ran onto the door, the walls, the stove and the breadbox. Rheumatoid arthritis had already deformed her hands during the years the paintings sold for a few dollars apiece to people stopping on the road. The house was later dismantled, restored and installed inside the Art Gallery of Nova Scotia, where it now stands as an exhibit in its own right.

moana-2016.gazette: The Oceanic Story Trust — Pacific historians, navigators, linguists and cultural practitioners — sat over the production from early development onward. Wayfinding as the film shows it is a real technique: reading star paths, swell direction and bird behaviour without instruments, a practice Polynesian navigators deliberately revived in the 1970s after generations of colonial rupture. Even the central mystery, a voyaging people who stopped voyaging, corresponds to an actual gap in the archaeological record.

neruda-2016.gazette: The Law for the Permanent Defense of Democracy outlawed Chile's Communist Party in 1948; Neruda, a sitting senator, lost his seat, went underground, and eventually crossed the Andes on horseback into Argentina. Larraín keeps that skeleton and fills it with invention, including a pursuing policeman who never existed. The fabrication is declared rather than concealed, which puts the film's distance from the record out in the open where it can be measured.
neruda-2016.prism: Declaring the invention is also a way of keeping control of it. The film admits it is making Neruda up, and in the same motion picks which parts of the record it will never have to answer for.

shin-godzilla-2016.gazette: Most of the running time is spent in conference rooms, with captions naming every ministry, committee and job title as the officials file in and sit down. That structure mirrors the crisis protocol Japan actually ran after March 2011: nested advisory bodies, deferred authority, a chain of approvals that had to complete before anything could move. The monster is barely the subject of the film; the delay is.

silence-2016.gazette: The Tokugawa authorities used the fumi-e — a bronze image of Christ or the Virgin, laid on the ground to be stepped on — as a bureaucratic test, administered, recorded and repeated on suspected Christians across Kyushu. Cristóvão Ferreira was real: the Jesuit provincial in Japan who apostatized under torture in 1633 and lived out his years in Nagasaki under a Japanese name. Endō built his novel directly on that case, and the film keeps its hard edge — the men who stepped left almost nothing behind in their own words.

the-salesman-2016.gazette: Farhadi opens with an apartment block buckling as excavation next door undermines it, a hazard familiar to anyone who has watched Tehran rebuild itself street by street. The displacement that follows, the landlord's silences, the way a private assault becomes a matter of neighbours and reputation — all of it runs on social codes the city genuinely enforces. He has worked this way since About Elly: no thesis, just the pressure a real system exerts on people who have to go on living inside it.
the-salesman-2016.prism: Realism cuts both ways under censorship. The codes the film observes so precisely are also the codes it had to satisfy to be released, and from outside it isn't always possible to tell which is which.
